content: I feel like this question is better suited to #Program verification. Unfortunately, I personally don't have any useful insight on your question, but I'm sure someone over there might

Hello I am part of a group of 6 people working on adding reflection on expressions on C++ standard.
Part of this working is defining the minimum set of features needed to be able to do at compile time analysis of c++ functions.
I would like to know what is the state of formal verification for C++ since it would allow us to verify that a meta-function like is_continuous<FN> would be correct.
I have not found any examples or tutorials that would allow formal verification of C++ code, let alone C++ code that heavily uses constexpr.
Could someone point me to where to begin such an endeavour of trying to formally verify certain of these functions using lean?
Maybe @Bas Spitters has some insight on this?
2 messages were moved here from #CSLib > reflection on expressions on C++ by Chris Henson.
(I combined the threads to prevent any confusion)

Bedrock/Bluerock was working on C++ in iris, so asking in the iris lean channel may be your best bet.
Quick googling, but there should be more...
